# Deep Research Intelligence Packet

## Cycle metadata

- Packet ID: `dr-20260926-1906-5-5-validation`
- Research system: `ChatGPT Deep Research`
- Started at: `2026-09-26 19:06 CDT`
- Completed at: `2026-09-26 19:09 CDT`
- Research scope: Direct-competitor customer and product-page mining
- Queue item or vendor: `competitor:5-5`
- Methodology: Four first-party 5&5 customer success stories were opened and assessed. Vendor-authored outcomes remain attributed claims and were not written into canonical records.

## Executive result

- Pages reviewed: 4
- Candidate pages validated: 4
- Brand-vendor-product observations added or revised: 4
- Company/competitor profile observations added or revised: 1
- Conflicts found: 2
- Material takeaway: 5&5 has named, product-specific implementation and managed-services evidence across Shipley Do-Nuts, Egg N Bird / FOMO Fries, Slice House, and Walk-On's. The pages show a hands-on role across Olo, Toast, Brink, Paytronix, Restaurant365, ezCater, and third-party delivery platforms, positioning 5&5 as a cross-platform restaurant technology implementation and operations layer rather than a core POS vendor.

## Evidence observations

### Observation 1

- Brand: Shipley Do-Nuts
- Vendor: 5&5
- Product or category: Olo online ordering; menu management; new-store digital setup; ownership-transfer workflow; web support
- Relationship indication: customer
- Deployment scope: enterprise
- Evidence type: case study
- Confidence: 95%
- Confidence rationale: 5&5's current first-party case study names Shipley, its operating context, Olo, the workflows managed, and the continuing support relationship.
- Source title: Shipley Do-Nuts | Stronger Systems. Smoother Operations.
- Source URL: https://5and5.com/success-stories/shipley-do-nuts/
- Publisher or source owner: 5&5
- Published date, if known: unknown
- Accessed date: 2026-09-26
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: 5&5 says it manages the full digital opening process for new Shipley shops, including location and ownership data collection, Olo configuration, menu accuracy, testing, and operator readiness; it also manages ownership transfers and ongoing menu and system changes.
- Product-specific evidence: Olo online ordering, menu configuration, ordering-flow testing, new-shop digital onboarding, ownership-change updates, website/web-sub maintenance, and franchisee communication.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The page is vendor-authored and does not provide an independent customer statement for every claimed workflow, a contract start date, or a precise current location count under management.
- Recommended follow-up: Confirm current Shipley scope, whether every shop is covered, and the specific ordering technologies referenced as new initiatives.

### Observation 2

- Brand: Egg N Bird / FOMO Fries
- Vendor: 5&5
- Product or category: Brink POS; Olo Rails; DoorDash, Uber Eats, and Grubhub activation; virtual-brand implementation
- Relationship indication: customer
- Deployment scope: enterprise
- Evidence type: case study
- Confidence: 95%
- Confidence rationale: 5&5's first-party case study names both brands and provides platform-level implementation detail, workflow, testing, and a stated sub-one-month launch timeline.
- Source title: FOMO Fries Case Study | Virtual Restaurant Tech Setup
- Source URL: https://5and5.com/success-stories/fomo-fries/
- Publisher or source owner: 5&5
- Published date, if known: unknown
- Accessed date: 2026-09-26
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: 5&5 reports configuring FOMO Fries' menu for POS compatibility, linking items to categories, modifiers, and reporting groups, and using Olo Rails to activate DoorDash, Uber Eats, and Grubhub storefronts with end-to-end order testing.
- Product-specific evidence: Brink and Olo implementation support, POS menu mapping, Olo Rails marketplace integration, storefront setup, direct order routing, and cross-platform testing.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The page does not identify the number of Egg N Bird kitchens participating, provide independent sales figures, or establish the virtual brand's current 2026 operating footprint.
- Recommended follow-up: Verify the current number of active FOMO Fries storefronts, whether Brink remains the POS, and which outcomes were measured after launch.

### Observation 3

- Brand: Slice House
- Vendor: 5&5
- Product or category: Toast POS management; Paytronix online ordering, loyalty, and gift cards; ezCater; Restaurant365
- Relationship indication: customer
- Deployment scope: enterprise
- Evidence type: case study
- Confidence: 95%
- Confidence rationale: The first-party page names Slice House's CTO, specific platforms and responsibilities, a 25-location impact statement, and an ongoing support relationship.
- Source title: Slice House Digital Transformation Case Study | 5&5
- Source URL: https://5and5.com/success-stories/slice-house/
- Publisher or source owner: 5&5
- Published date, if known: unknown
- Accessed date: 2026-09-26
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: 5&5 says it audited and standardized Slice House's Toast databases, implemented role-based permissions, led Paytronix online-ordering, loyalty, and gift-card work, coordinated marketplace migration, and supported ezCater and Restaurant365.
- Product-specific evidence: Toast database cleanup and ongoing management; Paytronix implementation and management; DoorDash, Uber Eats, and Grubhub migration coordination; ezCater and Restaurant365 implementation support.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The page reports growth from five to more than 25 locations and 100-plus development commitments, but these are vendor-published statements and development agreements are not operating units.
- Recommended follow-up: Confirm current live-location count, platform coverage by location, and whether all planned migrations are complete.

### Observation 4

- Brand: Walk-On's Sports Bistreaux
- Vendor: 5&5
- Product or category: Paytronix loyalty; Olo online ordering; implementation project management and testing
- Relationship indication: customer
- Deployment scope: enterprise
- Evidence type: case study
- Confidence: 95%
- Confidence rationale: 5&5's case study names the brand, platforms, implementation activities, six-month timeline, 80-location impact, and a named brand executive testimonial.
- Source title: Walk-On's Case Study | Sports Bar Technology Solutions
- Source URL: https://5and5.com/success-stories/walk-ons/
- Publisher or source owner: 5&5
- Published date, if known: unknown
- Accessed date: 2026-09-26
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: 5&5 says it led the Paytronix loyalty and Olo ordering implementations through configuration, training, menu and modifier setup, metadata work, QA, troubleshooting, and structured rollout support across an 80-location impact scope over six months.
- Product-specific evidence: Paytronix automatic-conversion loyalty model and guest FAQ; Olo menu, modifier, and metadata configuration; QA, testing, troubleshooting, training, and rollout project management.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: Reported improvements in participation, repeat visits, order completion, and guest satisfaction are not accompanied by numeric baselines, measurement periods, or independent validation.
- Recommended follow-up: Confirm whether 5&5 remains engaged after handoff, the live location count, and quantified pre/post loyalty and ordering outcomes.

## Company / competitor profile observations

### Competitor profile observation 1

- Target: `competitor:5-5`
- Field: synopsis
- Value or observation: 5&5 operates as a restaurant-focused implementation and managed-services layer across brands' existing technology stacks. The reviewed work spans POS cleanup and management, online ordering, loyalty, delivery marketplace activation, new-store setup, franchisee coordination, QA, and ongoing cross-vendor support.
- Confidence: 90%
- Confidence rationale: Four separate first-party customer stories consistently describe this cross-platform operating model with named brands and products.
- Source title: Shipley Do-Nuts; FOMO Fries; Slice House; Walk-On's success stories
- Source URL: https://5and5.com/success-stories/
- Publisher or source owner: 5&5
- Published date, if known: unknown
- Accessed date: 2026-09-26
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: Across the four pages, 5&5 repeatedly describes itself as implementing and operating third-party restaurant platforms on the brand's behalf, including Olo, Toast, Brink, Paytronix, Restaurant365, ezCater, and major delivery marketplaces.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The evidence is vendor-authored and does not establish market share, customer retention, or comparable performance against Genius.

## Negative findings

- Candidate or claim: 5&5 is itself a core POS software vendor.
- Pages checked: All four pages in the source ledger.
- Result: Unsupported. The pages instead show implementation, configuration, project management, and ongoing support for third-party platforms such as Toast, Brink, Olo, Paytronix, and Restaurant365.
- Candidate or claim: Vendor-reported outcome improvements can be treated as independently measured causal results.
- Pages checked: All four pages in the source ledger.
- Result: Unsupported. The pages provide qualitative outcomes and some scope/timeline figures, but no controlled attribution or independent measurement methodology.

## Source ledger

| URL | Source type | Accessed | Supports observation(s) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| https://5and5.com/success-stories/shipley-do-nuts/ | case study | 2026-09-26 | 1 | Productive; current Olo and digital-operations scope, but exact covered-location count is unstated. |
| https://5and5.com/success-stories/fomo-fries/ | case study | 2026-09-26 | 2 | Productive; Brink, Olo Rails, and delivery-platform implementation detail. |
| https://5and5.com/success-stories/slice-house/ | case study | 2026-09-26 | 3 | Productive; Toast, Paytronix, ezCater, and Restaurant365 work across a stated 25-location impact. |
| https://5and5.com/success-stories/walk-ons/ | case study | 2026-09-26 | 4 | Productive; Paytronix and Olo implementation across a stated 80-location impact and six-month timeline. |

## Research notes and inferences

- Inference: 5&5's competitive threat is services-led control of restaurant technology rollouts and ongoing operations, potentially influencing vendor selection and implementation success even when it does not own the underlying POS or SaaS products.
- Inference: 5&5 appears strongest where a brand has a fragmented multi-vendor stack or limited internal implementation capacity; the reviewed pages do not establish proprietary platform lock-in.
